 Judgment
The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for
the injuries and damages sustained by the petitioner in the alleged road traffic accident dated
04.

2. The petition averments in brief are as under:
On 04.11.2022 at about 5.15 p.m. the petitioner was returning from his place of work in motor cycle bearing No. KA-05-LK-8977 on Bangalore- Mysore road, near Gerupalya, at that time the driver of Tata- Intra goods vehicle bearing No.
KA-05-AL-3352 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner in the opposite direction, on the wrong side of the road and dashed against the motor cycle of the petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Atreum Speciality Hospital,
Bengaluru wherein he was admitted as inpatient.
Later he was shifted to Fortis Hospital, Bangalore and he has spent Rs.20,00,000/- towards hospitalization charges, treatment medicines, conveyance, nourishing food and other incidental charges etc.,

Prior to the accident, petitioner was very hale and healthy and he was working as Quality Check Executive in M/s. No Broker Technologies Solutions Pvt.
Ltd., Bengaluru and earning Rs.45,000/- per month.

sentences.text: Due to the accidental injuries petitioner is not able to continue his work and is under complete bed rest and he is suffering from permanent disability.

The respondent No.1 is the insurer of the goods vehicle bearing No. KA-05-AL-3352,
respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle bearing No. KA-05-AL- 3352 and respondent No.3 is the insurer of the motor cycle bearing No. KA-05-LK-8977
are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, prays to award compensation of Rs.1,20,00,000/- with interest.
3. After service of notices, respondent No.2 the owner of vehicle bearing No. KA-05-AL-3352 remained absent hence, placed exparte.
The respondent No. 1 & 3 insurance companies appeared through their counsel and filed written statement.

sentences.text: Respondent No.1 - insurance company appeared through its counsel and filed written statement by admitting the issuance of policy to the goods vehicle bearing No. KA-05-AL-3352 and the liability of this respondent, if any, is subject to proof of the policy.

This respondent has specifically denies the occurrence, mode of the accident and also involvement of goods vehicle bearing No.
KA-05-AL-3352.
The respondent No.1 contended that the driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.

Further denied the age,
avocation, alleged disability and income of the petitioner.
It is also contended that the alleged accident is caused by the negligence of the petitioner himself and the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, the respondent No.1 insurance company prays to dismiss the petition against it.

Respondent No.3 - insurance company appeared through its counsel and filed written statement by admitting the issuance of policy to the motor cycle bearing No. KA-05-LK-8977 and the liability of this respondent, if any, is subject to proof of the policy.

The respondent No.3 contended that the petitioner being the owner of motor cycle bearing No. KA-05-LK-8977 cannot maintain the petition against them as the accident is caused by the negligence of driver of vehicle bearing No.
KA-05-AL-3352.
Further denied the age, avocation, alleged disability and income of the petitioner.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, the respondent No.3 prays to dismiss the petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligent driving of Tata Intra goods vehicle bearing No. KA-05-AL-3352 by its driver, in RTA took place on 4.11.2022 at about 5.15 p.m. on Bengaluru- Mysore road, near Ramohalli cross, Gerupalya, Kumbal- agudu?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount & from whom?
3 . What order or award?
5. In order to prove the claim petition, the petitioner examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to 11.
Dr. S.Ramachandra, Senior Consultant Orthopaedic Surgeon at General Hospital, Jayanagar is examined as PW.2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.12 to 14.
The respondents have not adduced rebuttal evidence.

6. Heard the arguments and perused the material evidence that are available on record.
7.
My findings on the above issues are as under.

Issue No.1 : In the affirmative;
 Issue No.2 : In the affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final orders Ajay Kumar .G.M vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158600814/

 ISSUE NO.1 :
8.
That by reiterating all the averments made in the petition, the petitioner has filed his affidavit in lieu of- examination in-chief, which is considered as P.W.1.

In support of his case, he has produced true copies of FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, IMV report, wound certificate, notice and reply and charge sheet which are marked under Ex.P.1 to 7.
9.
On perusal of Ex.P1- FIR is registered on the basis of Ex.P2 first information given by the father of the petitioner.
The contents of Ex.P2 & 1 is in consonance with the contents of petition about the rash and negligence driving of the vehicle bearing No. KA-05-AL- 3352.
Ex.P3 is mahazar drawn by the police at the time of investigation.
On perusal of the contents of Ex.P3 spot mahazar, the accident spot within the five feet from the left side edge of the road in which the petitioner was proceeding.
It is alleged that the driver of vehicle bearing No. KA-05-AL-3352 who came from opposite side of the petitioner came to his extreme right side and dashed against the vehicle of the petitioner.
As per Ex.P3, at the time of mahazar, the IO has also found the blood stains within the five feet western side road edge.

Further the Ex.P4 is the IMV report where the vehicle bearing No.
KA-05-AL-3352 has got damaged in its front side and also the motor cycle of the petitioner also got damaged in its front side.

As per Ex.P3 mahazar, the accident is in the left side portion of the road where the petitioner was proceeding and as per the Ex.P4 IMV report, the front portion of both vehicles has got damage which evidentiates that the driver of vehicle bearing No. KA-05-AL-3352 came from opposite side of the petitioner came to wrong side and dashed against the motor cycle of the petitioner.

The contents of Ex.P3 & 4 prima- facie helped the petitioner to prove the alleged negligence of vehicle bearing No. KA-05-AL-3352.
10.
The Ex.P5 is wound certificate and Ex.P9 being the discharge summary wherein supported the case of the petitioner.
The contents of Ex.P5 and Ex.P9 corroborates with the contents of complaint.

Ex.P7 charge sheet is filed against the driver of the offending Tata intra goods vehicle bearing No.
KA-05-AL-3352 for the offence punishable under Sec. 279 & 338 of IPC.

By producing these documents, the petitioner prima-facie established the occurrence of accident and also the alleged negligence of the driver of the offending driver of tata goods vehicle bearing No. KA-05-AL-3352.
11.

Wherefore in the absence of any cogent evidence which could rebut the assertions made by PW-1 on oath supported by Ex.P-7 which is the charge sheet and the documents annexed therewith, this court should not have any impediment to conclude that the said documents prima-facie suffice to hold that accident, occurred due to rash and actionable negligence on the part of the driver of Tata intra goods vehicle bearing No. KA-05-AL-3352.

The view taken by this Court that the police records are prima- facie proof in support of the case of the petitioner, is supported by the decision rendered in Kishan Gopal and another Vs. Lala and others reported in 2013 (4) T.A.C 5 (S.C.), wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has categorically held thus:

sentences.text: In view of the aforesaid facts, the Tribunal should have considered both oral and documentary evidence referred to supra and appreciated the same in the proper perspective and recorded the finding on the contentious issue No. 1 & 2 in the affirmative.

But it has recorded the finding in the negative on the above issues by adverting to certain statements of evidence of AW-1 and referring to certain alleged discrepancies in the FIR without appreciating entire evidence of AW-1 and AW-2 on record properly and also not assigned valid reasons in not accepting their testimony.

The Tribunal should have taken into consideration the pleadings of the parties and legal evidence on record in its entirety and held that the accident took place on 19.07.1992, due to which Tikaram sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the same and the case was registered by the Uniara Police Station under Sections 279 and 304-A, IPC read with Sections 133 and 181 of the M.V. Act against the first and second respondents.

The registration of FIR and filing of the charge- sheet against respondent Nos.1 & 2 are not in dispute, therefore, the Tribunal should have no option but to accept the entire evidence on record and recorded the finding on the contentious issue Nos.1 and 2 in favour of the appellants.
(Emphasis supplied by me)

It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the inc ident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.

sentences.text: Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

Further the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105, where the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka considering the fact that the rider of the offending vehicle was not examined to prove any contributory negligence on the part of scooterist held that the accident had occurred due to rash or negligent driving by the rider of the offending van.

sentences.text: 12. In view of the ratio laid down in the authorities referred to above and applying the settled principle of law to the case at hand, which is further supported by the oral and documentary evidence adduced by PW-1, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the accident leading to this case indeed occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of tata intra goods vehicle bearing No. KA-05-AL-3352 resulting in petitioner sustaining injuries.
During the course of cross examination of petitioner, except a suggestion nothing has been elicited so as to disprove the case of the petitioner.
There are no material evidence to prove that the petitioner's negligence was the reason for the said accident.
In spite of sufficient opportunity, the respondents have not lead any evidence to rebut the case of the petitioner.

sentences.text: As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.

All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 4.11.2023 which is caused by the driver of the Tata intra goods vehicle bearing No.KA- 05-AL-3352 which belonging to respondent No.2.
There is no reasons to discard the evidence of petitioner.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
Accordingly, issue No.1 answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2:
14.
As already held herein above, the petitioner has proved that he has sustained injuries in RTA which is caused by respondent No.1.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads.
a) PAIN AND AGONY:-
At the time of alleged accident the petitioner was aged about 26 years.
The petitioner has not produced Aadhaar card.
But as per the available records in the file i.e., the copy of Aadhaar card and driving licence of the petitioner the date of birth of the petitioner is 5.7.1996.
The date of accident is 4.11.2022.
As such, as on the date of accident, the petitioner was aged about 26 years 3 months 30 days.
As per the wound certificate marked at Ex.P5 the age of the petitioner is shown as 25 but in the discharge summary marked at Ex.P9, the age of the petitioner is shown as 26 years.

As per Ex.P5 wound certificate the petitioner was admitted to Atreum Hospital on 4.11.2022 and discharged on 5.11.2022 and as per the discharge summary marked at Ex.P9 petitioner was admitted to Fortis Hospital on 5.11.2022 and discharged on 17.11.2022

it shows that he sustained post traumatic fracture left proximal humerus, comminuted intra articular fracture of left distal humerus, right distal radius + ulna fracture + druj instability and left distal radius + ulna fracture with druj instability.
As per the wound certificate marked at Ex.P5, the petitioner sustained totally four injuries which are grievous in nature.
By considering the nature of the injuries and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident Rs.1,00,000/- may be awarded to the petitioner under this head.
b) Medical expenses:
The petitioner has produced medical bills as per Ex.P11, amounting to Rs.9,72,565/-.
Out of the said amount, as per sl. no.1 bill marked at Ex.P11 i.e., Fortis Hospital bill dated 18.11.2022 is of Rs.7,10,155/-.

In the said Fortis Hospital bill of Rs.7,10,155/-, Rs.4,00,000/-
was paid by New India Assurance Co. Ltd., and only Rs.3,10,155/- was paid by the petitioner.
The petitioner also in the cross- examination stated that he has received Rs.4,00,000/- from his health insurance towards his inpatient bill.
Hence, only Rs.3,10,155/- has to be considered in the fortis hospital bill dated 18.11.2022.
The other bills produced by the petitioner also need to be reimbursed.
These bills are not disputed by the respondents and no grounds are made out to disbelieve these bills.
Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case in combined with the alleged injuries, the petitioner is entitled by rounding off the same i.e., Rs.5,72,565/- under this head.

sentences.text: The entries in the account statement of the petitioner shows that till 30.11.2022 he has received the salary.
The date of accident is 4.11.2022.
Thereby the petitioner has received the salary for the month of November, 2022.
As per this document, the gross income of the petitioner is taken as per offer letter as Rs.35,550/- p.m.
In the month of November the petitioner has got full salary credited to his account.
But December 31 st 2022 to he has left the job on 12.6.2023 he has received the lesser salary out of Rs.35,550/-.
Hence, by considering the laid up period of 4 months, the petitioner is entitled for the compensation by deducting the amount which he got as salary.
The evidence available on record shows that the petitioner has got total four grievous injuries.
By considering the same, the petitioner has taken six months of time for his recovery.
Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,89,341/- under this head.

d) Disability;- To prove the nature of injuries sustained by him the petitioner examined Dr.
Ramachandra, working as Sr. Consultant in Orthopedics at General Hospital, Jayanagar as PW.2,
through him clinical notes and X-ray are marked at Ex.P.12 to 14.

According to the evidence of this witness the petitioner sustained poly trauma- left ATA ( Anterior tibial artery) traumatic injury,
fracture's of comminuted intra articular left distal humerus - right distal radius+ ulna + druj ( Distal radius ulnar joint) instability and left distal radius+ ulna with druj instability.

He underwent debridement with exploration of left distal humerus with A/E ( above elbow) slab applied and right closed reduction + B/E ( below elbow) slab application, debridement with exploration left ankle and left ATA to DPA ( Dorsalis Pedis Artery) interposition graft with primary suturing.
The recent examination of the petitioner shown that the few fractures are united and few fractures are mal union.
The recent X-ray and CT scan films with report produced at Ex.P14 evidentiates the said mal union also.
The PW.2 examined the petitioner for assessment of disability.

sentences.text: The disability assessed by the PW.2 is only a physical disability and not functional disability.
As per the evidence available on record marked at Ex.P8 the petitioner completed his B.E. Civil Engineering in the year 2018.
Thus, the petitioner being educated was working as Quality Check Official at No broker Technologies Solutions Pvt. Ltd.,

entities.text: No broker Technologies Solutions Pvt. Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The education qualification of the petitioner shows that he was doing the desk job but certainly the four grievous injuries will impact on the working capacity of the petitioner to some extent.
Hence, I hold that the petitioner sustained disability of 18% to the whole body.
The petitioner has produced his Aadhaar card and driving licence which are available in the record and as per the said document, the petitioner was born on 5.7.1996.
The accident was occurred in the year-2022.
So, as on the date of the accident the petitioner was aged 26 years.
As per Sarala Verma's case, the proper multiplier applicable to the age of petitioner is '17'.
Hence, I inclined to award future loss of income at Rs.35,500 /- X 12 X 17 X 18% =Rs.13,05,396/- which is the total loss of future income.

The said amount is rounded off to Rs.13,05,400/-
e) FOOD, NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE;
As per Ex.P9 discharge summaries, the petitioner took treatment as inpatient for a period of 14 days.
As per wound certificate marked at Ex.P5 the injuries sustained by the petitioner are grievous in nature.
By considering the nature of the injuries and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident.
Hence looking to the treatment taken by the petitioner and injuries sustained he is entitled for compensation of Rs.70,000/- towards food and nourishment, conveyance.
f) ATTENDANT CHARGES:
The petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the accident.
The petitioner has spent 14 days in the hospital and there is no evidence or pleading in this regard to show that the petitioner is in need of attendant.

But by considering the nature of the injuries as discussed above, it may be considered to award attendant charges at Rs.1,000/- per day i.e.,
Rs.14,000/- in total.
g) Towards loss of amenities and enjoyment of life:
The petitioner admitted to the hospital for the injuries sustained by him, which might certainly have deprived him of the basic comforts and enjoyment.
The Ex.P5 wound certificate shows that the petitioner sustained with four grievous injuries.

Therefore,
it is just and proper to award a reasonable sum of Rs.80,000/- under this head.
h) Towards future medical expenses: The evidence of PW.2 doctor reveals that even though the fractures of the petitioner is union and some are mal union the implants are in situ.
Hence, it is evident that the petitioner is in need of an another surgery for removal of implants.
As per Ex.P5-there is four injuries.
By considering the same and also by keeping the future medications, surgeries and hospitalisation charges for removal of implants, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.60,000/- under this head.

sentences.text: The petitioner in his examination in chief stated that he has purchased his motor cycle KA-05-LK-8977 for Rs.3,80,000/- and after the accident he has received only Rs.2,78,000/ by the insurance company and remaining Rs.1,20,000/- was not paid by the insurance company.
In the chief-examination the petitioner stated that he has sold the said vehicle as it is fully damaged.
In this regard, the petitioner has not produced any documents to show the value of the vehicle and also the amount paid by the insurance company.
As stated by him, the petitioner has sold his motor cycle without proper any evidence it cannot be considered that the petitioner sustained loss due to the damages caused to his vehicle.
The details of the repairs of his vehicle or the person who purchased the vehicle is not examined before this tribunal.
No evidence is available to show that the petitioner has sold his motor cycle and it is severely damaged.
Hence, he is not entitled for the damages under this head.

15. Liability:-
According to the petitioner the respondent No.1 is the insurer of the goods vehicle bearing No. KA-05-AL-3352, respondent No.2 is the owner of the said goods vehicle.

The respondent No.3 is the insurer of the motor cycle bearing No.
KA-05-LK- 8977.
As per the reasons discussed in issue No.1, the accident is caused by the negligence of driver of goods vehicle bearing No. KA-05-AL-3352.

Hence, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner and the respondent No.1 insurance company shall indemnify the compensation on behalf of the respondent No.2.
The petitioner is entitle for compensation with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
Accordingly, this issue answered in the affirmative.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for total  compensation amount of Rs.23,91,306/-
(Rupees Twenty three lakhs ninety one thousand three hundred and six only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The respondent No.1 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
The case against respondent No.3  stands dismissed.

Out of total compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner, 75% of the same to be released in favour of petitioner through E- payment on his proper identification and remaining 25% to be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank, for a period of three years, in his name.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw up award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.issue:
4. On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:
1.
Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligent driving of Tata Intra goods vehicle bearing No. KA-05-AL-3352 by its driver, in RTA took place on 4.11.2022 at about 5.15 p.m. on Bengaluru- Mysore road, near Ramohalli cross, Gerupalya, Kumbal- agudu?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount & from whom?
3 . What order or award?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
By producing these documents, the petitioner prima-facie established the occurrence of accident and also the alleged negligence of the driver of the offending driver of tata goods vehicle bearing No. KA-05-AL-3352.
11.
Wherefore in the absence of any cogent evidence which could rebut the assertions made by PW-1 on oath supported by Ex.P-7 which is the charge sheet and the documents annexed therewith, this court should not have any impediment to conclude that the said documents prima-facie suffice to hold that accident, occurred due to rash and actionable negligence on the part of the driver of Tata intra goods vehicle bearing No. KA-05-AL-3352.
The view taken by this Court that the police records are prima- facie proof in support of the case of the petitioner, is supported by the decision rendered in Kishan Gopal and another Vs. Lala and others reported in 2013 (4) T.A.C 5 (S.C.), wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has categorically held thus:
Ajay Kumar .G.M vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158600814/
4
In view of the aforesaid facts, the Tribunal should have considered both oral and documentary evidence referred to supra and appreciated the same in the proper perspective and recorded the finding on the contentious issue No. 1 & 2 in the affirmative.
But it has recorded the finding in the negative on the above issues by adverting to certain statements of evidence of AW-1 and referring to certain alleged discrepancies in the FIR without appreciating entire evidence of AW-1 and AW-2 on record properly and also not assigned valid reasons in not accepting their testimony.
The Tribunal should have taken into consideration the pleadings of the parties and legal evidence on record in its entirety and held that the accident took place on 19.07.1992, due to which Tikaram sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the same and the case was registered by the Uniara Police Station under Sections 279 and 304-A, IPC read with Sections 133 and 181 of the M.V. Act against the first and second respondents.
The registration of FIR and filing of the charge- sheet against respondent Nos.1 & 2 are not in dispute, therefore, the Tribunal should have no option but to accept the entire evidence on record and recorded the finding on the contentious issue Nos.1 and 2 in favour of the appellants.
Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed
The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.
During the course of cross examination of petitioner, except a suggestion nothing has been elicited so as to disprove the case of the petitioner.
There are no material evidence to prove that the petitioner's negligence was the reason for the said accident.
In spite of sufficient opportunity, the respondents have not lead any evidence to rebut the case of the petitioner.
Ajay Kumar .G.M vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158600814/
5 13.
As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.
All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 4.11.2023 which is caused by the driver of the Tata intra goods vehicle bearing No.KA- 05-AL-3352 which belonging to respondent No.2.
There is no reasons to discard the evidence of petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads.
At the time of alleged accident the petitioner was aged about 26 years.
Ajay Kumar .G.M vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158600814/
6 c) Loss of income during laid up period:
Hence, by considering the laid up period of 4 months, the petitioner is entitled for the compensation by deducting the amount which he got as salary.
The disability assessed by the PW.2 is only a physical disability and not functional disability.
The education qualification of the petitioner shows that he was doing the desk job but certainly the four grievous injuries will impact on the working capacity of the petitioner to some extent.
Hence, I hold that the petitioner sustained disability of 18% to the whole body.
By considering the nature of the injuries and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident.
opennyai_summary.arguments: It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the inc ident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Thus, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
a. Towards pain and agony Rs. 1,00,000/-
b.
Towards medical expenses Rs. 5,72,565/- c.
Towards loss of income during Rs.
1,89,341/-
laid up period d.
Towards disability Rs. 13,05,400/-
e.
Towards food, nourishment and Rs. 70,000/-
conveyance f.
Towards attendant charges Rs. 14,000/- g.
Towards loss of amenities Rs. 80,000/- h.
Towards future medical expenses Rs. 60,000/-
I.
Towards vehicle and general NIL  damages  Total Rs.23,91,306/-
15. Liability:-
Hence, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner and the respondent No.1 insurance company shall indemnify the compensation on behalf of the respondent No.2.
The petitioner is entitle for compensation with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
Accordingly, this issue answered in the affirmative.
For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for total  compensation amount of Rs.23,91,306/-
(Rupees Twenty three lakhs ninety one thousand three hundred and six only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The respondent No.1 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
The case against respondent No.3  stands dismissed.
Out of total compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner, 75% of the same to be released in favour of petitioner through E- payment on his proper identification and remaining 25% to be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank, for a period of three years, in his name.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw up award accordingly.
